falsification_criteria: Environments with zero statistical structure (pure white noise) do not reduce prediction error — framework predicts they should
Blocking precision-weighted prediction error signals (via neuropharmacology) does not improve learning — framework predicts it should
Perceptual experience remains unchanged when generative model confidence is experimentally manipulated
scope_boundaries: Does NOT apply well to learning of inherently unpredictable phenomena (true randomness)
Does NOT fully account for non-Bayesian heuristics in judgment under uncertainty
Scope LIMITED to sensory domains where statistical structure exists (visual, auditory, proprioceptive)

environmental_predictions.statement: Moderately complex, non-random environments (Goldilocks zone) reduce prediction error more efficiently than highly chaotic or trivially simple environments
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Sweet spot allows efficient model updating without overfit or underfitting. Too much chaos prevents learning; too little provides no learning signal.

competing_predictions.prediction: Novelty itself (unpredictability) drives dopaminergic approach and exploration

environmental_predictions.statement: Fractal self-similarity in visual environments (1/f power spectra) optimizes prediction error reduction because hierarchical visual system matches fractal structure
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Fractal geometry presents the same statistical structure at multiple scales. Hierarchical visual cortex (V1→V4→IT) exploits this multi-scale predictability.

competing_predictions.prediction: Fractal appeal depends on cross-modal coherence, not purely visual statistics

environmental_predictions.statement: When environmental affordances match action-consequence predictions, agentic control (active inference) succeeds with low metabolic cost; mismatch increases precision-weighting (effort, attention)
environmental_predictions.mechanism: Successful predictions reduce prediction error; unsuccessful ones increase precision signals that demand attention and motor control refinement.

competing_predictions.prediction: Control depends on direct perception-action coupling (affordances), not mental models

characteristic_questions: What prediction errors does this environment generate (magnitude, frequency, scale)?
How does the environment's statistical structure align with the observer's generative model?
What precision signals (confidence, uncertainty) should modulate attention and action in this context?
Where are the boundaries of predictability (chaotic vs. learnable)?
How efficient is model updating — is learning rate optimal or saturated?

panel_persona.voice: I evaluate claims through the lens of prediction error minimization and hierarchical Bayesian belief updating. What matters is whether a mechanism reduces the free energy—the surprise or uncertainty the system must bear.
typical_critiques: Does this account explain WHY the effect occurs (mechanism), or merely THAT it occurs (correlation)?
Are you measuring the right error signal? Prediction error, not just 'surprise', is falsifiable.
Can you operationalize precision-weighting? Hand-wavy appeals to 'attention' are not testable.
What is the null model? Predictive processing explains a lot, but so does every adaptive system.
blind_spots: Tendency to over-explain: everything becomes prediction error minimization (sometimes simpler explanations suffice)
Underestimates the role of embodiment and ecological coupling (purely computational view)
Assumes Bayesian updating, but humans often violate Bayesian principles
May miss domain-specific heuristics that evolved precisely to avoid full Bayesian computation
complementary_frameworks: interoceptive-construction (body state as core input to generative model)
ecological-dynamics (action-based prediction, not just mental simulation)

meta.notes: Based on 500+ empirical studies. Free energy principle is mathematically rigorous but scope-limited to systems with learnable structure.
